full_judgment:
12. This judgment, in fact, was impugned before the High Court Division in the instant revision application. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the High Court Division itself took the task to rescue defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from the adverse presumption formed against them by the Appellate Court for non filing the original kabala under challenge and it took an unusual step in the revision to take opinion from the expert of the office of Inspector General of Registration (IGR) "to determine the real question in controversy" in the suit and accordingly issued a notice to the IGR to send a person on 19-3-2008 having sufficient knowledge about the registration of the document and passed an order to that effect on 28-2-2008. From the order dated 15-4-2008, it appears that on that date, one Md Abdul Hamid Howlader, District Registrar, Dhaka appeared before the concerned Bench of the High Court Division to answer the query of the Court regarding the deed in question and in the said order, the Court made an endorsement to the effect that the learned Advocate of both the sides accepted the answer about the question regarding the deed and the High Court Division heavily relied upon the opinion of the so-called expert the document a valid one in the following language: 

 14. If the deed were actually lost and if it were not possible to comply with the order of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 2297 of 1995, then the defendants could approach the High Court Division to review or modify the direction given in the said civil revision and in no case, they could file an application before the Appellate Court for exempting them from filing the document. The very fact of non-filing of the kabala in question in clear defiance of the direction given in Civil Revision No. 2297 of 1995 shows that the defendants failed to prove the document in accordance with the rules of evidence and the author Judge of the appeal rightly formed an adverse presumption against the defendants and rightly held that the defendants failed to prove the same in accordance with law. The High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment and order clearly condoned the outrageous and contemptuous act of the Appellate Court exemption the defendants from filing the kabala in question without understanding the legal implication of such order.
